Member (Hannah Morrison): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Hannah Morrison, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Morrison): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.

Member (Hannah Morrison): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Hannah Morrison): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Hannah Morrison): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Hannah Morrison): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Hannah Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Hannah Morrison): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Hannah Morrison): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Hannah Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000056.transcript:
Member (Fatima Ahmed): I was approved for this weeks ago and I still haven't been reimbursed.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Fatima Ahmed, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): I changed banks last month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let's find out where that payment went.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): It was a massage therapy claim for 120 dollars.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How were you expecting to be paid?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Direct deposit, like all my other claims.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did you update it through the app or with your employer?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Through my employer's payroll. I didn't know Sun Life was separate.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have any other claims come through since you switched?
Member (Fatima Ahmed): No, this is the first one since.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've checked the payment history and the direct deposit details on file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Sun Life keeps its own direct deposit details, separate from your employer's payroll, so a change at work doesn't carry over.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm checking where the payment was sent and whether it came back.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The payment was issued to the account on file on the 12th. I can open a trace, but it takes up to ten business days.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): So I just wait again?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry, yes. The trace is open, and I've set a reminder to check it next week.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Can you call me when it's found?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've asked for a call-back once the trace is complete, and you'll also see it in the app.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: a payment trace is open, it can take up to ten business days, and you'll get a call when it's done.
Member (Fatima Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Chen): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Liam Chen, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Chen): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Liam Chen): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Liam Chen): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Liam Chen): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Liam Chen): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): How much medication do you have left?

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Liam Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The prior authorization form is on file from last week. It just wasn't linked to the drug claim. I've linked it, and the pharmacy can resubmit today.
Member (Liam Chen): So I can pick it up today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Yes. The authorization is linked to the claim now, so the pharmacy can resubmit and it should go through.
Member (Liam Chen): Will I have to do this every time?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): No. It's approved for twelve months, so refills go through automatically.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So you're all set: the authorization is on file for twelve months and the pharmacy can process it today.
Member (Liam Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Leila Cote): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.

Member (Leila Cote): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Leila Cote): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Leila Cote): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Leila Cote): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000120.transcript:
Member (Leila Campbell): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Leila Campbell, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Campbell): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Leila Campbell): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Leila Campbell): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): How old is he?
Member (Leila Campbell): Fourteen.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Leila Campbell): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Leila Campbell): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Leila Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Leila Campbell): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Leila Campbell): Great, that helps.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Leila Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Mathieu Roy, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mathieu Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Mathieu Roy): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Mathieu Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Mathieu Roy): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mathieu Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Mathieu Roy): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Mathieu Roy): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Mathieu Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent Daniel Okafor compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

SL-000166.transcript:
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Gurpreet Fortin, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): When did you go off work?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Martin): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Noah Martin, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Martin): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Noah Martin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Tyler Wilson): My medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.

Member (Tyler Wilson): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Tyler Wilson): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Tyler Wilson): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which pharmacy are you using?

Agent (Marc Tremblay): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Tyler Wilson): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Tyler Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

SL-000531.transcript:
Member (Hannah Roy): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Hannah Roy, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah Roy): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah Roy): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Hannah Roy): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Hannah Roy): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Hannah Roy): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Hannah Roy): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Hannah Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Hannah Roy): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Hannah Roy): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Hannah Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Morrison): The receiving institution says they never got anything.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Arjun Morrison): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Arjun Morrison): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Daniel Okafor): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Daniel Okafor): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Arjun Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Lucas Patel): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Lucas Patel, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Patel): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Lucas Patel): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Lucas Patel): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Lucas Patel): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Lucas Patel): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Lucas Patel): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Lucas Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Lucas Patel): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Lucas Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Lucas Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Lucas Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Tyler Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Lavoie): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Olivia Lavoie): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Olivia Lavoie): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Olivia Lavoie): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Olivia Lavoie): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?

Member (Chantal Chen): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Chantal Chen, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Chen): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Chen): Yes, that's right.
Member (Chantal Chen): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?

Member (Chantal Chen): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.

Member (Chantal Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Chantal Chen): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Chantal Chen): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Chantal Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Leila O'Brien): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): How old is he?
Member (Leila O'Brien): Fourteen.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Leila O'Brien): No, this is the first time.

Member (Leila O'Brien): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.

Member (Leila Patel): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Leila Patel, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Patel): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Leila Patel): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Leila Patel): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Leila Patel): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Leila Patel): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Leila Patel): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Leila Patel): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Leila Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Leila Patel): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Leila Patel): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Leila Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): Hi Emma Patel, Daniel Okafor here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Daniel Okafor): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.

Member (Emma Patel): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?

Member (Emma Patel): Fourteen.

Member (Emma Patel): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Emma Patel): Great, that helps.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Emma Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah O'Brien): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Hannah O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Hannah O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Hannah O'Brien): Yes, that's right.
Member (Hannah O'Brien): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Hannah O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Hannah O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Hannah O'Brien): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Hannah O'Brien): They said they billed it the same way as always.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Hannah O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Hannah O'Brien): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Hannah O'Brien): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Hannah O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Tyler Kim): I'm following up again — I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Tyler Kim, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Kim): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Tyler Kim): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Kim): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Tyler Kim): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Tyler Kim): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Tyler Kim): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Member (Tyler Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Tyler Kim): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Tyler Kim): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Tyler Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Chen): I'm following up again — my medication claim was put on hold for more information and I don't know what you need.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Olivia Chen, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Chen): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Olivia Chen): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Olivia Chen): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Olivia Chen): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Olivia Chen): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?
Member (Olivia Chen): I told them, and they said they'd need the form itself from Sun Life.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): How much medication do you have left?
Member (Olivia Chen): About four days. That's why I'm calling now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the information request and the documents already on file.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Olivia Chen): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Olivia Chen): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Olivia Chen): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Olivia Chen): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Fatima Morrison): I'm following up again — my dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Fatima Morrison, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Morrison): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Fatima Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.

Member (Fatima Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
